ReaderView.dc.html.title: S3 · What you read in the report

t1.text: Account: one unticked box for pictures

n1.text: New on A and B: the second box, Share pictures of cards I correct. Never ticked from the start, and not needed to continue: only the terms box unlocks the button. Asked once per account; after that it lives in Settings. The fine print is new: To find and fix problems, Mesa notes how the app is used and any errors. No ads, and no pictures unless you choose. On B a short What's new box says why the terms changed.

n2.text: Settings is new: Home's menu had only Sign out. The switch saves at once, with no Save button. Off means nothing new is kept from that moment. Delete removes every report and picture the player has sent, whatever the switch says, and leaves the switch as it is. No green toast: the result is written in place (F).

t3.text: Where the button sits, and what it is called

v1.text: V1 wins: nothing new on screen. It sits where people look for help (the menu) and where camera trouble shows (the panel). Loses: two clicks, and a player who never opens either won't find it.

v2.text: V2 wins: one click, always in sight, so every player learns it exists. Same label everywhere: Report a problem. On the phone it sits in the top bar beside Disconnect, not as a floating button that can be hit while placing the phone. Loses: one more control on the top bar.

t4.text: The report: what went wrong, which card, Send

n4.text: Nothing is required: Send works with no note and no tag, because the 10 minutes are the report. One tag at a time; tap again to clear. The sentence about what is sent changes when the phone is gone (L) and on the phone (M). The phone never sends by itself: a tap there asks the computer to send the same package (N), and says so when it can't (O). The code is a receipt the player needs, not an ok toast.

n5.text: The table the prompt calls section 4 is section 2 in today's privacy.html (section 4 is transfers). The draft changes sections 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7, and the version line. Anthropic is not changed: no new way sends pictures to Claude. Legal basis per row and the sentence about trained models are for Jesper to approve.

n6.text: G2: seven categories that match what goes wrong on the mat. Pointing at the card in the picture frozen at the press tells the reader which card. Wrong name asks what the card is called. It happened: Just now or Earlier tells the reader where in the 10 minutes to look. Only the category picks are new; Send still works with nothing filled in. States H to O get the new texts once G2 is chosen.

t6.text: Which card, and when: point at it

r1.text: R1 wins: tap first, then say what is wrong; the choices follow where you tapped (a card only in the camera can only be Didn't show up). A pin shows on both pictures, so the reader sees the same card twice. Loses: only shows the moment of the press; a problem that already went away can't be pointed at.

r2.text: R2 wins: everything in R1, plus a strip of the last minutes. Drag back to when it looked wrong and point there. Handles a duplicate that flickered and went away, or a card you already fixed. Loses: one more row; the mat in the strip comes from the computer's own history, the camera pictures from the phone's stills (MES-366), fetched when the box opens.

r3.text: R3 wins: no pictures to search; a list of what Mesa did, with your own fixes marked. Tap the line that went wrong. Very exact for the reader. Loses: a card that never showed up is not in the list (needs the camera picture below), and a list is harder to scan than a picture during a game.

t6b.text: New version: one problem, mark any cards

s1.text: S1: three steps, same order every time. 1 What went wrong (one category). 2 Which cards: tap any number, in the camera picture and on the mat, each picture on its own; numbers follow the order you tap. The strip picks the moment. 3 Anything to add, where the numbers can be used. One report is one problem; several problems are several reports (Report something else after sending). Nothing is linked between the pictures and nothing is asked per card, so there are no special cases. Only Wrong name asks one more thing: what the card is called.

s3.text: S3 is not something the player sees. It is the top of LÄS-MIG.md that dev/rapport/hamta.cjs writes (MES-365): category, the moment, every mark with its track and what Mesa did with it, the note, and the events around the moment. The marks turn the player's numbers into track ids, so the note can't be misread.
